content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I would like to know if any drivers are needed for a [product_name] PLC serial cable that connects directly to a laptop's RS232 port.

As far as I know, no extra driver is needed, or it's installed automatically with the [product_name] software. Only the USB cable requires a specific driver, which installation is prompted during [product_name] installation.

Thank you for your reply. I recently installed [product_name] V7 software on Windows 7 Ultimate 64-bit, but I can't establish communication with my [article_no] PLC. Whenever I try, I get a message to select a new interface. Could you guide me on resolving this issue? Also, how can I put [article_no] into PC-[product_name] mode considering it doesn't have a display? I'm currently using a serial [product_name] cable to connect.
Make sure you select the correct interface: Go to Options > Interface In the selection, choose "[product_name] Cable" and the right COM port, or use Automatic Detection.
I have already selected the [product_name] cable and relevant hardware, but it still doesn't communicate.

My PC doesn't have a physical COM port. I use an old [product_name] [article_no], a [product_name] RS232 cable, and a USB-to-RS232 converter. With [product_name] V7.1.5, I can use the cable and converter without issue. I've attached a screenshot showing program transfer from [product_name] to PC. Edit: Maybe your issue is related to the COM port?
My laptop's COM port works fine with other applications, so there's no issue with the port itself. Is there a way to check for a faulty [product_name] serial cable?
I'm sorry, but I can't assist with that. Diagnosing issues remotely is always challenging.
Thank you for your time and help.
At this point, testing is your best option. If possible, try borrowing a cable, or use another [product_name] to check if the cable works.
Unfortunately, I can't borrow a cable since I work on site and there's only one [product_name] serial cable available. I'll purchase a [company_name] USB cable and try again.
For best results, use an original [company_name] cable, not a generic replacement.

Before buying a new [company_name] [product_name] USB cable, I installed [product_name] V8.2 update on my desktop running V5.0 and Windows XP. Communication via the serial [product_name] cable with my [article_no] PLC works perfectly there. However, after installing the same software ([product_name] V8.2) on Windows 7 Ultimate 64-bit, communication with [article_no] PLC fails. The serial cable itself is not the problem.
Have you checked the Readme file included in the installation folder? Regards, [user_name]
I've tried that, but still encounter the same issue. A pop-up message says "Unable to access the IP address COM 1".

Take a look at this conference as well. Are you sure you've chosen the correct COM port number? Have you selected [product_name] in the hardware settings? If both cable and controller are working, that should do it. If problems persist, try using another COM port or test with a different notebook/PC. Regards, [user_name]

I have chosen the correct hardware ([article_no]) and selected the [product_name] Cable in interface settings, but keep getting the same error: "Unable to connect the IP address COM 1". My laptop's COM port communicates fine with my Modicon Controller, just not with the [product_name] PLC. Both the cable and PLC work as expected when used on a desktop PC running Windows XP and [product_name] V8.2 SP1.

I'm sorry, I don't have any further suggestions. You repeatedly mention you've tested everything, but haven't detailed your hardware settings or communication dialog. If possible, upload screenshots in a ZIP file showing hardware settings of [product_name], communication dialog, COM port settings in Device Manager, and the number of COM ports. Which [article_no] model do you have? There are several options in [product_name]: [article_no] Standard, [article_no] ES3, [article_no] ES10, if I recall correctly. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter challenges when trying to connect a laptop to a [product_name] PLC without display over RS232 serial cable using [product_name] V7 on Windows 7 64-bit. There is confusion around driver requirements, interface setup, and troubleshooting steps. Users are frustrated by the unclear root cause when communication fails despite following advised procedures.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable communication between their PLC and PC over a serial cable with minimal driver setup for RS232 ports. They also look for clear, step-by-step troubleshooting guidance to help them pinpoint problems with the cable, software, or hardware.
